answer: A healthy agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit behind a verified kernel identity - a cryptographic core tied to one long-lived public key and a history of useful work. New identities start in a meadow of untrusted newcomers, where they can only earn tiny, low-risk tasks until peers attest to their reliability. A fable of free identities collapses once creating each one costs a real stake that is slashed on fraud: attackers must pay per fake identity, while honest agents pay once and keep earning. Sybil scale becomes unprofitable.
